title: Cobertura do verificador numérico de gradientes KN-003
hypothesis: A seleção de coordenadas do checkGradients, filtrada por gradiente analítico não nulo, pode omitir um grupo inteiro cuja retropropagação tenha sido zerada por regressão.

baseline_observation.limitation: No per-group assertion when the candidate coordinate list is empty.

candidate_design: Select deterministic coordinates from every one of the 14 parameter arrays regardless of analytic gradient magnitude; include zero and non-zero analytic gradient coordinates.

For each parameter array, add a seeded random-direction directional-derivative check: compare the central finite difference along a normalized direction against the dot product of the analytic gradient and that direction.
Run more than one seed and headCount values 1, 2 and 4 using valid even head dimensions.
Vary context lengths and include EOS as a supervised target.
Sweep several finite-difference epsilons in float32 and look for a stable error plateau rather than assuming smaller epsilon is always better.
Report coordinate counts, directional errors and max absolute/relative error per parameter array.
controls: Use same model implementation/configuration/seed between baseline and candidate.
Use central finite differences with explicit epsilon and identical numerical tolerances.
No production weights, checkpoints, tokenizer format or app runtime changes.
Use centered finite differences for all numerical comparisons.
Report absolute error for near-zero gradients; relative error must handle the both-zero case explicitly and must not hide small but materially different gradients.
Keep forward/loss deterministic and avoid changing optimizer or training state during perturbations.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 14 ParameterSet arrays has at least one coordinate finite-difference check, including zero/non-zero analytic values where present.
Every one of the 14 arrays passes at least one seeded directional-derivative check.
All sampled numerical/analytic values are finite.
Absolute and relative errors remain within predeclared, precision-calibrated tolerances over a stable epsilon range.
Gradle neural/unit suite passes on unchanged baseline and candidate.
A negative-control mutation that removes one parameter group's analytic gradient is detected by the checker.
risks: Finite-difference noise in float32 for near-zero derivatives.
Broader configurations may expose genuine math defects or require calibrated tolerances.
status_note: This is a test-coverage hypothesis, not a discovered incorrect model gradient. The experiment has not been executed.

research_basis.note: CS231n lecture 6 slide 64 advises centered differences, scale-aware relative comparison, explicit both-zero handling, awareness of float32 and epsilon, and checking selected coordinates in every separate parameter tensor.
PyTorch documents central finite differences and warns that defaults are designed for double precision and may fail with lower-precision inputs.
JAX check_grads uses a single randomly selected direction to reduce numerical-check cost; adapt as an additional directional check per tensor group, not as a replacement for coordinate coverage.
